raw_response:
I’m 58 this year, and I’ve farmed Quzhou land a long time. I don’t like making big changes unless I’ve seen them work. On my 10.9 mu, I’ll still keep most land in wheat-maize because that is the steadiest way to get grain and cash, and I’ll leave a smaller piece for cotton so I’m not relying on one crop only. I have well water, so I can protect the crop at key times, but pumping costs money, and some family members work outside, so I can’t manage too many fussy operations. The extension guy talks about exact rates, but in practice I still go by what the field looked like last year, what neighbors are doing, and what I can afford in hand. For wheat I’ll feed it a bit heavier because wheat responds well here; maize I’ll plant right after wheat harvest with simple field prep because the turnaround is tight; cotton I’ll keep on a smaller area because it takes more watching and picking.
